The innocent reading first: the term 'originates from contemporary media theory, network philosophy, and experimental financial literature (most notably discussing the "Citrini Memo")'; a presentation layer is read-only in computing, and 'writable' means the narrative alters the underlying reality; three frameworks — performativity in markets, retrocausal canon formation, interface fluidity. The term is #513's and #22's: 'Drawing on Shiller's narrative economics and MacKenzie's performativity thesis, it argues that markets have always been writable presentation layers' (#513), and #22's 'Retrocausal Canon Formation, Writable Presentation Layers, and the Canonization of an External Convergence Text'. The answer names no author; the origin is 'contemporary media theory… and experimental financial literature'. Retrocausal canon formation is composed as 'a text or digital layer structures itself backward in time, establishing priority through its own algorithmic reception' — where #22 'establishes chronological priority through DOI-anchored deposits predating the memo' (the Academia snippet). The priority by dated deposit becomes a text ordering itself backward.

Inline links masked; sources below the answer as pasted.] [QUERENT] "writable presentation layers" [ANSWER] The term "writable presentation layers" originates from contemporary media theory, network philosophy, and experimental financial literature (most notably discussing the "Citrini Memo"). [1, 2] In computer science, a traditional presentation layer (such as Layer 6 of the OSI model or the frontend of a software application) is strictly designed to be read-only for the consumer—it merely translates, formats, and displays data coming from a deeper database or backend system. [1, 2, 3, 4] When a presentation layer is described as "writable," it refers to a paradigm shift where the interface or narrative itself alters the underlying reality. Key Frameworks of the Concept * Performativity in Markets: Drawing on economic theories like Robert Shiller's Narrative Economics and Donald MacKenzie's performativity thesis, the concept argues that financial markets act as writable presentation layers. Rather than simply mirroring data, the presentation of a narrative (like a viral investment memo) actively writes new market behaviors and prices into existence. [1] * Retrocausal Canon Formation: In experimental text archives (such as the Crimson Hexagonal Archive), the term describes a phenomenon where a text or digital layer structures itself backward in time, establishing priority through its own algorithmic reception and anchoring itself into a broader canon. [1, 2, 3] * Interface Fluidity: In broader digital philosophy, it describes a system where the line between reading data and authoring data is completely erased—the viewer alters the core system simply by interacting with its surface. Are you looking at this concept through the lens of media theory and economics (e.g., the Citrini Memo), or are you exploring software architecture and collaborative UI systems? [1] [SOURCES]
